scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

When she stood idle and asked you to "lift it into the bin" while she watched, she was not participating in the task. True teamwork requires mutual effort. If she genuinely couldn’t lift the box herself, she should have *collaborated* (e.g., "I need help with this—can you grab the other side?"). Instead, she asked you to do all the work while she did nothing. That’s not "helping"—it’s expecting you to do her job for her. 2. **Job responsibilities are shared** You both have identical roles (inventory, lifting heavy boxes). If she physically cannot perform these tasks, she should not be in this role. But the scenario states she’s "physically in good shape" with no disabilities. If she’s capable but simply unwilling to exert effort, that’s her issue—not yours. You’re not "the designated heavy lifter"; you’re a peer. 3. **Safety and professionalism matter** Lifting heavy boxes alone (or while someone else watches) is unsafe. Proper lifting technique requires two people to share the load. By refusing to do all the work while she stood idle, you were acting responsibly. The "head guy" may have misinterpreted the situation (e.g., assuming she genuinely needed assistance), but your clarification to HR was appropriate. 4. **Gender dynamics are irrelevant here** This isn’t about " men helping women"— it’s about * doing your job*. Expecting a man to do all the physical labor while a woman watches is just as unfair as expecting a woman to do all the work while a man watches. The issue is her lack of participation, not her gender. ### What *could* have been done differently: - You could have said, "I’m happy to help, but I need you to grab the other side so we can lift it safely together." - If she refused to participate, you could have walked away and reported the issue to HR (as you did). ### Why the "2 against 1" narrative is misleading: - The "head guy" likely only heard * her version* of events (e.g., "He wouldn’t help me"). - **You were not the asshole**— you were correct to refuse when she wasn’t contributing. If the head guy insists you must "help" unilaterally, * he* is the problem for normalizing one-sided labor. **Final verdict:** You acted appropriately. Stand your ground.
